title: Diffusionless mechanisms produce diffusion-like electrochemistry in battery particles
abstract: Published online: 17 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02123-5 Overpotentials at low frequencies in Li-ion battery active particles have long been attributed to solid diffusion. Now, electrolyte penetration in battery agglomerate particles is shown to make interior surfaces electrochemically active, but with a transmission-line configuration. This mechanism for accessing battery capacity produces diffusion-like electrochemistry, even without diffusion involved.

title: Electronic conductivity of solid electrolytes causes physical self-discharge in <mark>all-solid-state</mark> batteries
abstract: Published online: 17 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02090-x Physical self-discharge critically limits the lifetime of <mark>all-solid-state</mark> batteries (ASSBs). Wang et al. showed that the non-negligible electronic conductivity of solid-state electrolytes can lead to substantial physical self-discharge in ASSBs.
